pairs.why: Both feeders are seen from similar slightly-elevated front views with a blurred park behind, and neither camera angle clearly differs from the real card.
A turns the locker about 30° with the door on the right and the top face showing, like the real card, while B mirrors it and sits lower.
A shows the real card's tilted, thick body with visible side depth and some perspective, while B reads as a flat panel seen nearly head-on.
B shows the ship in three-quarter view from the bow with a foreshortened bowsprit and visible deck, closer to the real card's depth, while A is a flat side elevation.
A has a moderate camera and orientation like the real cap, with the visor pointing lower-left on planks, while B uses a closer, wide-angle view with exaggerated perspective.
Both anchors are near-frontal, with the crossbar mostly flat to the picture plane, and neither reproduces the real card's tilted, foreshortened crossbar.
B turns the table slightly and shows more of the top surface and ground depth, closer to the real card's high, rotated view, while A is nearly symmetric and frontal.
A shows the real card's chunky body thickness at the lower edge and a similar tilt toward the viewer, while B is a thin, flat slab.
